biography.plain_text: Pietro Marzotto was an Italian industrialist who led his family's textile group into international fashion, acquiring businesses including Hugo Boss and Valentino. The youngest son of Gaetano Marzotto, he studied law in Milan. After selling his stake in the family company, he acquired Peck, the historic Milanese delicatessen and food business.

long_biography.plain_text:
Textile industrialist Pietro Marzotto brought trade-union representatives to the Hannover fair to examine new looms in 1978. Before proceeding with the purchase, he discussed the machinery with them and accepted that changes to workers' duties would also need negotiation. The representatives had endorsed the new equipment as an advance.

His negotiations could be difficult as well as direct. During a forty-eight-hour dispute over working hours in 1977, he pressed for a productivity condition, tore up the proposed agreement and walked out. Within minutes, he apologised and signed. He also held an annual meeting with managers and union representatives.
